About the Scholarship

The Schiavon scholarship supports journalism research at Melbourne. It is linked to research-degree admission and the award's subject requirements. Applicants should check the course admission dates and scholarship selection process, because a separate fixed closing date was not stated in the checked information.

Research Areas

  • Research methods
  • Doctoral research

About University of Melbourne

Melbourne offers research degrees across its faculties and graduate schools. Named research scholarships can carry subject or background criteria in addition to the requirements for doctoral admission.

Official details: Read the programme or project information

Application route: Follow the official application instructions

Contact

Questions about this position, eligibility or the application process should be raised through the contact channel given on the official announcement page (see the Official Link section above). Always quote the position reference in your message so the admissions or HR team can route your enquiry quickly.

Official Link

Full announcement and application portal: https://scholarships.unimelb.edu.au/awards/schiavon-journalism-research-scholarship

Source: scholarships.unimelb.edu.au - the details in this listing were recorded from this official page.

Important Notes

  • Application deadline: No separate fixed deadline stated - late or incomplete applications are normally not considered.
  • Listing details were recorded from the official source at the time of publication; always confirm the latest requirements on the official page before applying.
  • Prepare the documents listed in the eligibility and application sections before starting the online form - transcripts, CV and references take the longest to collect.

How to Apply

Submit your application through the official portal before the deadline: No separate fixed deadline stated; course admission dates apply. Read the eligibility requirements carefully and prepare all requested documents — early applications are strongly recommended for competitive awards.
